🇮🇳 India’s $4 TRILLION gold 🧈🧈🧈 wealth effect may be one of the most underappreciated macro stories. 

Indian households own 25,000 tonnes of gold — worth $3.9 trillion, 𝙪𝙥 𝙖𝙣 𝙚𝙭𝙩𝙧𝙖𝙤𝙧𝙙𝙞𝙣𝙖𝙧𝙮 ~$2 𝙩𝙧𝙞𝙡𝙡𝙞𝙤𝙣 𝙞𝙣 𝙟𝙪𝙨𝙩 2 𝙮𝙚𝙖𝙧𝙨

That means that the value of gold held by Indians is almost 100% of GDP

Some striking numbers:

 🌕 Gold is now ~24% of household wealth, versus just ~6% in equities

🏦 Household gold is worth ~2x bank deposits and ~4x equities

💰 Organised gold loans have surged from $86bn → $197bn in 3 years, a ~32% CAGR

📈 Yet gold loans are only 5.1% of household gold value, below 5.9% two years ago — gold prices have risen faster than monetisation

💳 Including informal lending, only ~15% of household gold may currently be monetised

📊 Gold ETF AUM has exploded from $2.8bn in Mar-23 → $18.5bn in Mar-26

Unlike equities, gold ownership extends deep into rural and lower-income India. Rising gold prices therefore create a potentially broader wealth effect.

If monetisation catches up, Jefferies estimates gold loans could rise another $15–20bn annually. And every further 10% rise in gold creates roughly $400bn of household wealth and potentially $20–25bn of additional gold loans.

That could translate into a  spending tailwind of 0.8% to 1% of GDP.

⚠️ But there is another side: India imported $79bn of gold in FY26 (~2% of GDP) versus $36bn in FY23. What strengthens household balance sheets can simultaneously worsen the current account.

Gold is therefore becoming more than a store of wealth in India — it is increasingly a transmission mechanism from global gold prices → household collateral → credit → consumption.

Source: Jefferies

🇮🇳 India’s $4 TRILLION gold 🧈🧈🧈 wealth effect may be one of the most underappreciated macro stories. 

Indian households own 25,000 tonnes of gold — worth $3.9 trillion, 𝙪𝙥 𝙖𝙣 𝙚𝙭𝙩𝙧𝙖𝙤𝙧𝙙𝙞𝙣𝙖𝙧𝙮 ~$2 𝙩𝙧𝙞𝙡𝙡𝙞𝙤𝙣 𝙞𝙣 𝙟𝙪𝙨𝙩 2 𝙮𝙚𝙖𝙧𝙨

That means that the value of gold held by Indians is almost 100% of GDP

Some striking numbers:

 🌕 Gold is now ~24% of household wealth, versus just ~6% in equities

🏦 Household gold is worth ~2x bank deposits and ~4x equities

💰 Organised gold loans have surged from $86bn → $197bn in 3 years, a ~32% CAGR

📈 Yet gold loans are only 5.1% of household gold value, below 5.9% two years ago — gold prices have risen faster than monetisation

💳 Including informal lending, only ~15% of household gold may currently be monetised

📊 Gold ETF AUM has exploded from $2.8bn in Mar-23 → $18.5bn in Mar-26

Unlike equities, gold ownership extends deep into rural and lower-income India. Rising gold prices therefore create a potentially broader wealth effect.

If monetisation catches up, Jefferies estimates gold loans could rise another $15–20bn annually. And every further 10% rise in gold creates roughly $400bn of household wealth and potentially $20–25bn of additional gold loans.

That could translate into a  spending tailwind of 0.8% to 1% of GDP.

⚠️ But there is another side: India imported $79bn of gold in FY26 (~2% of GDP) versus $36bn in FY23. What strengthens household balance sheets can simultaneously worsen the current account.

Gold is therefore becoming more than a store of wealth in India — it is increasingly a transmission mechanism from global gold prices → household collateral → credit → consumption.

Source: Jefferies

reports.text:
GUFIC BIOSCIENCES | SPECIALTY INJECTABLES & CDMO TRANSFORMATION

Business Profile
- Revenue base: ~₹940 Cr.
- Historically focused on CMO and domestic pharma.
- Business is shifting towards specialty injectables, CDMO and global markets.
- ~80–85% of revenue comes from injectables.
- Strong presence in lyophilized/freeze-dried injections.
- Products span antibiotics, antifungals, fertility hormones, cardiac drugs and antivirals.
- Exports to 50+ countries.

Specialty Business Portfolio
- Complex injectable manufacturing.
- IVF and fertility hormones.
- Botulinum Toxin.
- APIs and domestic formulations.
- International exports.
- CMO/CDMO opportunities.
- Combination of niche businesses creates multiple growth avenues.

Botulinum Toxin | Emerging Opportunity
- One of India's few indigenous Botulinum Toxin businesses.
- Gufic is the only Indian manufacturer of Botulinum Neurotoxin.
- Brands include STUNNOX and ZARBOT.
- Currently contributes ~3.5% of revenue.
- Indian market estimated at ₹120–130 Cr.
- Market remains heavily import-dependent.
- Small contribution today but significant potential if domestic penetration increases.

IVF & Fertility
- Portfolio includes 40+ SKUs.
- Covers HCG, HMG and FSH.
- Indian ART/IVF drug market estimated at ~₹4,000 Cr.
- Developing differentiated and recombinant hormone alternatives.
- Fertility portfolio provides another specialised growth avenue.

Indore Facility | Biggest Earnings Lever
- Investment of ~₹350–360 Cr.
- Facility faced a ~2-year delay.
- Interest, depreciation and employee costs impacted profitability before meaningful revenue ramp-up.
- Q4 FY26 utilisation reached ~30%.
- EBITDA breakeven achieved.
- Facility could now shift from earnings drag to earnings driver.

Capacity Reallocation
- CMO activity being shifted to the Indore facility.
- Frees Navsari capacity for higher-value products.
- Additional capacity available for branded products.
- Export products can also utilise the freed capacity.
- Improves potential overall product mix.

Indore | Global Manufacturing Platform
- Facility built to US-FDA/EU-GMP standards.
- Positioned for international exports.
- Supports complex injectable manufacturing.
- Creates a platform for CDMO expansion.
- International regulatory standards can improve access to global customers.

CDMO Opportunity
- Gufic is increasingly targeting global CDMO opportunities.
- GLP-1 validation batches executed for a large global pharma client.
- Production carried out at the Indore facility.
- Successful validation could support future commercial opportunities.
- New capacity provides room for higher-value contract manufacturing.

Gufic Ireland | Europe
- Gufic Ireland secured its first EU Marketing Authorisation in 2026.
- Creates a direct route into the European market.
- Strengthens the company's international platform.
- Can support future product launches and market expansion.

Margin & Earnings Inflection
- Indore reached EBITDA breakeven at ~30% utilisation.
- Further utilisation can improve operating leverage.
- Higher volumes can spread fixed costs across a larger revenue base.
- Potential progression:
  Utilisation ↑ → Revenue ↑ → Margins ↑ → Cash Flow ↑

Key Concerns
- Indore project was delayed by ~2 years.
- Original ₹1,500 Cr revenue ambition is difficult to reconcile with current trajectory.
- EBITDA margin declined from ~18.1% in FY24 to ~16.3% in FY26.
- Execution remains an important monitorable.
- New capacity needs to translate into sustained revenue and cash-flow growth.

THE TRANSFORMATION
- CMO + Domestic Pharma
  → Specialty Injectables
  → IVF / Botulinum Toxin
  → Global Exports
  → Complex Injectables
  → CDMO Platform

KEY TAKEAWAY
- Gufic is not yet a fully scaled specialty-pharma/CDMO business.
- The central thesis is the transition from investment phase to harvesting phase.
- Indore is the key variable in this transformation.
- EBITDA breakeven at ~30% utilisation is an important milestone.
- CDMO, exports, IVF and Botulinum Toxin provide additional optionality.

KSH INTERNATIONAL | COPPER IS THE PASS-THROUGH, EBITDA/TONNE IS THE STORY

Business Model
- Manufactures copper winding wires for transformers and motors.
- Reports business in two buckets.
- Specialized winding wires.
- Standard winding wires.
- No separate EV or T&D reporting segment.
- Copper largely passes through the P&L.

How To Read The Business
- Copper is procured after customer orders are received.
- Pricing is linked to prevailing LME copper prices.
- Higher copper prices inflate reported revenue.
- Revenue growth alone can therefore be misleading.
- EBITDA/tonne is the key operating metric.
- Core framework: Tonnes × EBITDA/tonne.

EBITDA/ Tonne | Key Metric
- Q1 FY26: ~₹66,000/tonne.
- Q4 FY26: ~₹74,000/tonne.
- Q1 FY27: ~₹93,000/tonne.
- FY27 comfort level: ~₹75,000/tonne.
- Q1 performance significantly exceeded the full-year comfort level.
- Sustainability of this level is the key monitorable.

Specialized Wires | Higher Value
- Specialized wires generate higher profitability than standard wires.
- CTC is the highest-value product within specialized wires.
- Q1 FY27 recorded a record CTC mix.
- Phase 1 capacity was front-loaded towards CTC.
- Phase 2 adds standard and EV capacity.
- Product mix expected to normalize over 2–3 quarters.

CTC | Core Strength
- CTC stands for continuously transposed conductor.
- Uses multiple thin enamelled copper strands.
- Strands are transposed to distribute current evenly.
- Conductors are additionally paper-wrapped.
- Primarily used in large power transformers.
- KSH holds a leading position in India's CTC market.

End-Market Mix
- ~75% of current business linked to large power transformers.
- Export contribution: ~27%.
- Exports were ~29% previously.
- Management targets exports at ~40%.
- Global transformer demand provides structural visibility.

Transformer Opportunity
- Global transformer OEMs reportedly hold 3–5 year order books.
- These are customer order books, not KSH's own order book.
- Five-year framework agreement signed with Hitachi Energy Global.
- Agreement does not specify quantity or pricing.
- Transformer demand provides long-term industry visibility.

Standard Wires | India Opportunity
- BIS is shifting imported standard wire demand towards Indian suppliers.
- Local sourcing can create additional domestic opportunity.
- Phase 2 capacity adds standard-wire capability.
- Mix shift can broaden the addressable market.

EV Opportunity
- 2W and 3W EV demand currently remains stronger.
- Passenger vehicles and buses are longer-dated opportunities.
- Meaningful passenger-car/bus opportunity expected around FY28–29.
- Phase 2 includes dedicated EV capacity.

Capacity Expansion
- Phase 1 was weighted towards CTC.
- Phase 2 expands standard and EV capabilities.
- New capacity increases addressable end markets.
- Product-specific capacity creates strategic flexibility constraints.
- Mix is expected to normalise as Phase 2 ramps up.

Capacity Allocation Risk
- Copper drawing capacity is relatively fungible.
- Insulation capacity is product-specific.
- CTC lines cannot manufacture EV wire.
- Each insulation line effectively commits capacity to an end market.
- Capacity decisions are made well ahead of demand.
- Typical lead time for such capacity decisions is ~18 months.

KEY TAKEAWAY
- Reported revenue is heavily influenced by copper prices.
- Revenue growth and EBITDA margin should not be viewed in isolation.
- The key framework is tonnes × EBITDA/tonne.
- Q1 FY27 EBITDA/tonne of ~₹93,000 materially exceeded the ₹75,000 FY27 comfort level.
- CTC currently drives superior economics.
- Transformer exposure remains the dominant business.
- Standard and EV capacity will change the product mix over the next 2–3 quarters.
- Export expansion towards 40% provides another growth lever.
- The key question is whether elevated EBITDA/tonne can remain sustainable.

Acquisition accelerates AXISCADES’ aerospace manufacturing strategy, combining immediate capability with planned capacity expansion at Devanahalli.

Earlier, a stock’s closing price was based on its VWAP during the final 30 minutes.

A fund could trade during this period, but it could not know in advance what the final closing price would be.

With CAS, closing orders are collected and matched at a single equilibrium price, helping index funds and ETFs trade closer to the same price used by their benchmark.

For F&O traders, this creates another interesting effect.

Large MSCI buy and sell orders will now enter the cash-market auction, while futures and options continue trading until 3:40 PM.

So large moves in affected stocks during CAS could also be reflected in Nifty and stock futures and options.

The important thing to remember is that nothing has necessarily changed in the companies themselves.

But if MSCI changes a stock’s place or weight in its indices, funds tracking those indices still have to buy or sell it.

So some stocks could see large flows during today’s CAS, purely because of an index change.

This is the first MSCI rebalance since the Closing Auction Session (CAS) was introduced in Indian markets.

And this is exactly the kind of situation CAS was designed for: allowing large closing orders from index funds and ETFs to be matched at the market’s actual closing price.

In the last rebalance, ETFs and index funds tracking MSCI had to adjust their holdings.

The additions were estimated to trigger around $1.38 billion of buying, while the deletions were estimated to lead to around $715 million of selling.

Overall, the rebalance was estimated to result in around ₹8,000–8,500 crore of net outflows from Indian stocks.

Its MSCI India Index tracks around 165 large and mid-sized Indian companies.

ETFs and other index funds then track these indices, just like Nifty ETFs track the Nifty 50.

So when MSCI adds or removes a stock, or changes its weight in the index, these funds have to adjust their holdings too.

That can lead to large buying or selling in the affected stocks.

India absorbed ~82.6 Mn sq ft of office space in 2025 - the third consecutive record year

In Q12026 alone, flex platforms accounted for ~26% of total office leasing, while GCCs contributed ~44% of Grade A absorption

A few interesting trends:

- Flex workspace stock is expected to cross 100 Mn sq ft by 2027, with penetration rising above 14%. Around 70-80% of flex demand is already enterprise led, while contract tenures have increased to 3-5 years versus 1-2 years earlier.

- GCCs are emerging as one of the biggest demand drivers. Around 40-50% of Grade A demand is expected to come from GCCs. 

- GCC flex leasing itself is expected to grow at ~28% CAGR through 2030, around 1.7x faster than other segments. Flex share within GCC leasing could rise from ~18% in 2025 to ~32% by 2030. 

Interestingly, AI could actually accelerate flex adoption. As companies find it harder to forecast headcount 5-10 years ahead, they increasingly prefer scalable offices with shorter commitments instead of locking themselves into long traditional leases. 

The broader office market is growing ~8%, flex is growing ~22%, while Smartworks grew ~24%

As of Mar'26, Smartworks had ~10.1 Mn sq ft operational area and ~16.1 Mn sq ft total footprint across 66 centres. More importantly, 100% of its FY27 building requirement is already secured and it has >75% visibility for FY28.

FPIs Want Direct Exchange Access - A Headwind for Brokers, Not the Capital-Market Theme

Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) are pushing SEBI for direct access to stock exchanges, seeking to bypass broker infrastructure and connect their trading servers more directly with the exchanges for faster execution. If permitted, this could mark a meaningful change in the way institutional trades are routed in India. 

For brokers, the development is clearly a potential structural headwind, particularly for businesses that rely heavily on institutional execution and transaction-linked revenues. Direct connectivity could reduce the intermediary’s role in the execution chain and increase competitive pressure on brokerage economics. 

Importantly, however, this is an FPI request being considered by SEBI - not a SEBI proposal that has already been approved or implemented.

The impact also shouldn't be extrapolated to the entire capital-market ecosystem. Exchanges could actually benefit if faster and more efficient access encourages greater FPI participation, liquidity and trading volumes, while depositories such as CDSL and market-infrastructure businesses such as KFin and CAMS are largely insulated because their core functions remain essential irrespective of how an order reaches the exchange.

In other words, this could be negative for the intermediary but potentially positive for the underlying market infrastructure. 

For investors tracking the capital-market theme, the development looks more like a potential shift in value within the ecosystem rather than a threat to the broader structural story of rising market participation, institutionalisation and financialisation of Indian savings.

BRENT CRUDE SURGES ABOVE $90 AS US-IRAN TENSIONS ESCALATE 🚨

🔺 Brent crude climbed above $90/barrel after the US military targeted Iranian rocket launchers allegedly preparing to deploy mines into the Strait of Hormuz.

⚠️ The report says this marks the first such US attack in more than a month, raising fresh concerns over disruption to the key oil-shipping route.

🚢 Around 6–8 million barrels of crude per day are reportedly still flowing through the Strait of Hormuz despite the absence of a US-Iran peace agreement.

🇺🇸 US forces say they are closely monitoring the waterway and remain prepared to safeguard the free flow of commerce.

🤝 Diplomatic hopes remain, with an Iranian official saying resuming diplomacy with the US “isn’t impossible” following discussions involving Qatar.

🔴 Impact: Negative for India — sustained crude above $90 can increase India's import bill, inflationary pressure and costs for oil-dependent sectors; positive for upstream oil producers.

Nomura on Infosys
Buy, TP Rs 1290
CFO meet takeaways
AI services opportunity could reach USD300-400bn by 2030E
CFO reemphasised six value pools in AI which Infosys believes will create meaningful demand in medium to long term
These pools include:
1) AI strategy & engineering (incl. agent build/orchestration),
2) data for AI (enterprise data readiness without sharing data broadly with foundation models),
3) Process AI (agentled process reimagination; customer service cited as a major wedge),
4) legacy modernization (AI-enabled acceleration),
5) Physical AI (AI embedded into devices/edge/autonomous systems) and
6) AI trust (security + responsible AI + compliance).
AI services continue to grow rapidly for company having risen from 5.5% in 3QFY26 to 8.2% in 1QFY27.
Infosys’ CFO believes that rising tech complexity in enterprises only makes the role of system integrators like itself more relevant given that it has a deep understanding of the clients’ processes and context which is hard to replace.

DAM Capital on Sugar Sector

Triveni Engineering - BUY, TP Rs415
Screens best because it barely feels that closure

Dalmia Bharat Sugar - BUY, TP Rs710
Holds cleanest beneficiary position

Balrampur Chini - BUY, TP Rs825
Is purest sugar play in coverage

Domestic sugar has repriced from Rs38-41/kg in June-2026 to Rs52-55/kg by end-August, with an ex-factory spike to Rs68/kg that drew government intervention: 1mn tonne of duty-free imports, a 15-day stockholding cap on bulk buyers & anti-hoarding action.
Prices cooled but have not gone back down
Imported sugar lands and refines at around Rs50/kg, and that cost is now the floor under the market.
Nothing cheaper arrives until 2mn tonnes India needs lands, likely by March-2027
Raise sugar realisation for FY27 and FY28 to Rs47/kg from Rs43-44/kg

Triveni Engineering - BUY, TP Rs415
Screens best because it barely feels that closure.
More than half its distillery capacity can switch to grain, allowing ethanol volumes to grow 17% to 250mn litres in FY27 at over 80% utilisation.
Crushing has fallen 12% over two seasons on Co-0238 infestation, but over 75% of its catchment has been replanted and we conservatively model a 5% uptick in crush.
Higher volumes at improving recovery drive 79.5% operating profit growth to Rs7.3bn in FY27.

Dalmia Bharat Sugar - BUY, TP Rs710
Holds cleanest beneficiary position.
It closed June with 230kt of inventory carried at Rs36.9/kg, lowest cost base in industry, against a spot market above Rs50/kg, &that gap converts directly into FY27 earnings.
Sector-leading recovery earns it upper end of the Rs6-8/kg industry spread, & its import contracting record should win it a large share of programme.
Ethanol volumes fall 14% to 160mn litres in FY27 before the Ramgarh dual-feed conversion restores them to 200mn litres
Estimate 54.6% operating profit growth to Rs 6.6bn in FY27.

Balrampur Chini - BUY, TP Rs825
Is purest sugar play in coverage.
Crushing rose 5% in SS26 and should rise again in SS27, with over 90% of its catchment replanted away from Co-0238, adding volume into a deficit market.
Distillery volumes fall roughly 25% to around 200mn litres, but sugar price benefit far outweighs that loss, driving 53.6% EBITDA growth in FY27, with PLA commissioning in Q3FY27 adding 23.6% in FY28.

Many Problem: Solar led grid instability / Energy import / Pollution One solution: EV India is winning solar race. Solar supply a huge chunk of daytime power, pushing net grid demand sharply lower arnd noon. But demand peaks after sunset. That's the classic "duck curve" problem

~80 GW swing created largely by renewable output. The irony: clean power is available when demand isn't. Several states doing solar curtailment as the grid couldn't absorb all midday generation. So, next phase of green transition is tougher than just adding more solar panels

India imports ~90% of its crude oil needs & roughly half of its natural gas . Energy security remains one of the biggest economic vulnerabilities. Crude oil is among India's largest import items. Every $ oil prices widens the import bill = trade deficit = pressure on Rupee

Air pollution remains a public health emergency in major metros. Delhi frequently records PM2.5 levels many multiples above WHO norms, while Mumbai too has seen worsening air quality episodes. Solar, oil imports & air pollution are not separate challenges. They are connected

The common link is urban transport. A large share of oil consumption in metros comes from ICE cars commuting daily between home & office. Think about office parking lots. Vehicles remain parked for 8-10 hrs during the exact period when solar generation is highest

What if every major office complex became a daytime EV charging hub? Cars would consume power when solar generation is abundant, helping flatten the duck curve instead of deepening it.

Corp can accelerate this shift. EV subsidy for employees & workplace chargin infra can become part of CSR spend (2% of PBT) Vehicles in metros spend most working hours parked at offices. Converting 20%+ of parking capacity into chargers can create a daytime demand for solar power

One solution. Multiple benefits. More EVs = lower oil imports, cleaner city air, higher daytime power consumption, better solar utilisation & stable grid. Sometimes the smartest energy storage isn't a battery plant. It's millions of parked EVs connected to chargers.

- Business has three major engines: Xanthine, API and CDMO.

🚢 SHIPBUILDING ANCILLARY SERIES 

Company # — Rappid Valves (India) Ltd | NSE: RAPPID 299

India’s shipbuilding story isn’t only about shipyards.

The bigger opportunity may sit with critical ancillaries supplying every vessel.

🔹 Rappid manufactures industrial & marine valves
🔹 Supplies into naval, shipbuilding & repair applications
🔹 Approved/registered with multiple Indian shipyards
🔹 ClassNK marine certification adds credibility
🔹 Moving beyond valves → valve + actuator + control-panel integration

🔥 Naval trigger

Recent orders linked to the Indian Navy Fleet Support Ship programme:

BHEL — ₹18.06 Cr
Shree Refrigerations — ₹8.55 Cr
Müller-BBM — ₹3.25 Cr

Total: ~₹29.85 Cr

Plus L&T — ₹2.84 Cr FSS-related order.

Executable order book: ~₹40 Cr, versus FY26 revenue of ~₹53 Cr.

📈 FY26

Revenue: ₹53.2 Cr
EBITDA: ₹10.3 Cr
PAT: ₹6.5 Cr

But there is a major red flag:

CFO: –₹10.8 Cr
Debtor days: ~170
Inventory days: ~258

So the thesis is NOT simply “order book = multibagger.”

I want to see:

Revenue growth + margin stability + positive cash flow + improving working capital.

If those start appearing together, Rappid could become an interesting small-cap naval shipbuilding ancillary to watch.

Series lesson:

> In India’s shipbuilding boom, don't just track who builds the ship. Track who supplies the critical components inside it. 🚢⚙️

Underappreciated SBI MF's distribution moat 

SBI MF's biggest advantage isn't fund performance. It's distribution. In India, bank-backed AMCs blessed with an edge as the bank branch is still the most powerful financial distribution channel
Investors trust banks with savings, salaries & FDs. Convincing a depositor to buy a bank-sponsored MF is far easier than acquiring a customer from scratch. Trust compounds over time
This trust factor is visible across the industry. 4 of India's top 5 AMCs are bank-backed. Even with rising competition, large AMCs have largely retained market share
SBI has the widest reach across the country, with one of the largest branch networks, customer bases & geographic presence among all financial institutions. That reach is difficult to replicate
Unlike most AMCs, SBI MF gets disproportionate support from its parent. SBI Bank contributes 35% of SBI MF's equity AUM. Compare that with just 8% for ICICI AMC & 6% for HDFC AMC
More interestingly, 40% of SBI MF's equity AUM comes through bank channels, versus 19% for ICICI AMC & 12% for HDFC AMC. SBI's distribution engine remains a major growth driver
Most banks operate open architecture & recommend products across AMCs based on suitability. SBI may have open architecture formally, but data suggests SBI customers get mostly SBI-branded investment products
The numbers are striking. 100% of SBI MF's promoter-bank sourced AUM sits with SBI, vs 70% for ICICI AMC & just 28% for HDFC AMC. That's about as captive as distribution gets
SBI's MF penetration opportunity is still huge. Average MF AUM per SBI branch is only ~10% of retail deposits per branch, implying a long runway for existing customers to migrate from deposits into MFs
The next leg of growth likely comes from B30 markets. SBI MF already has the highest B30 equity AUM share at 16%, ahead of ICICI AMC (12%) & HDFC AMC (11%)
SBI's deep Tier-2/Tier-3 presence matters. 66% of SBI MF's SIPs originate from B30 markets, giving it access to underpenetrated investors who are just beginning their financialization journey
The final edge is economics. SBI MF's distribution cost through SBI is just 65 bps, lower than HDFC AMC's 68 bps & ICICI AMC's 69 bps. Better reach + higher trust + lower cost = a distribution moat that's hard to disrupt

The Relationship Trump Misunderstood:
For three decades, China and emerging markets effectively exported disinflation to the developed world. They produced goods at a fraction of Western costs and shipped them to consumers in the US and Europe. The result: lower prices and higher purchasing power
The West got cheaper TVs, phones, clothes, furniture and industrial goods. China got manufacturing jobs, export growth and rising incomes. It wasn't a one-way relationship. Both sides benefited
As exports surged, China accumulated enormous foreign exchange reserves. Every dollar earned from exports added to a growing pool of savings that had to be invested somewhere
Those reserves served two purposes: protect the yuan from volatility and build strategic national wealth. China used them to buy foreign assets, resources, companies and financial securities around the world
A large portion of those reserves found their way into US Treasuries. China became one of the largest lenders to the US government, recycling export earnings back into America's financial system
This mattered because sustained Treasury demand helped keep long-term US interest rates lower than they otherwise would have been. Cheap imports lowered inflation. Treasury purchases lowered financing costs
In effect, China was helping on two fronts: suppressing goods inflation through low-cost manufacturing and supporting bond markets through reserve recycling. 
Trump focused heavily on one side of the equation: the trade deficit. From that perspective, China was exporting too much and manufacturing jobs were leaving America. This became the basis for tariffs and trade confrontation.
But the other side received less attention. Those same imports were keeping prices low for US consumers. Many products became affordable precisely because they were manufactured in lower-cost economies
The relationship also extended to capital markets. China's reserve accumulation created a steady source of demand for US government bonds, helping support the broader financial system
Today that world is changing. China is no longer a low-income economy desperate for export growth. Wages have risen, technology has improved and its economic influence is far greater than it was 20 years ago
The old model of unlimited cheap labour, ever-rising globalization and automatic reserve recycling is fading. Both countries increasingly view the relationship through a strategic lens rather than purely an economic one
As supply chains fragment and tariffs rise, the US may face more inflation from its own policy choices. Producing goods domestically or through alternative supply chains is often more resilient, but rarely cheaper
At the same time, if foreign demand for Treasuries becomes less predictable, bond investors may demand higher yields to absorb increasing government debt. Higher yields mean higher financing costs across the economy
The next decade may look very different from the last three. Less globalization, more strategic competition, potentially higher inflation and structurally higher interest rates. Markets are still figuring out what that world looks like
Bottom line: The US-China relationship wasn't simply buyer vs seller. It was a system where goods, capital and inflation dynamics were deeply intertwined. Breaking that system may create consequences on both sides.
